url:https://emcrit.org/emnerd/a-study-in.significance: This has significant implications for ICU clinical practice, as it may lead to the adoption of ineffective treatments and delay the discovery of effective ones.

url:https://rebelem.com/hfnc-vs-niv/.summary: This study compared high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) to non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in patients with acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema. It found that HFNC may be as effective as NIV in reducing respiratory rate and improving respiratory distress within 2 hours. The study aimed to determine if HFNC is a viable alternative to NIV in this setting.
url:https://rebelem.com/hfnc-vs-niv/.significance: This study's findings could help clinicians choose between HFNC and NIV for patients with acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema, potentially improving patient outcomes and reducing the need for invasive ventilation.

url:https://litfl.com/ecg-criteria-for-l.summary: This study reviews the ECG criteria for diagnosing left ventricular hypertrophy, including their historical development, diagnostic performance, and limitations. It aims to provide a comprehensive overview of these criteria for clinicians. The study covers the principal ECG criteria used to diagnose left ventricular hypertrophy.
url:https://litfl.com/ecg-criteria-for-l.significance: Understanding ECG criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy is crucial for accurate diagnosis and management of cardiac conditions in ICU patients, allowing for timely interventions and improved patient outcomes.

url:https://emcrit.org/emnerd/the-case-o.summary: The YEARS protocol was tested to see if it can safely identify low-risk patients with suspected pulmonary embolism. The study aimed to determine if this approach can be applied to patients with malignancy. Results were not provided.
url:https://emcrit.org/emnerd/the-case-o.significance: This study's findings could impact ICU clinical practice by helping clinicians determine which patients with malignancy and suspected PE can safely use a lower D-dimer threshold.

url:https://emcrit.org/emcrit/racc-lit-2.summary: This is a literature review on various topics in critical care, including prehospital whole blood transfusions, defibrillator damage from DSD, and adenosine dosing for supraventricular tachycardia.
url:https://emcrit.org/emcrit/racc-lit-2.significance: Understanding these topics can help ICU clinicians make informed decisions and improve patient outcomes.

url:https://litfl.com/cant-intubate-cant.summary: This study discusses the management of Can't Intubate Can't Oxygenate (CICO) situations in ICU, where standard airway rescue techniques fail. CICO is recognized, and the patient is prepared for Front of Neck Access (FONA). FONA is then transitioned to for oxygen delivery.
url:https://litfl.com/cant-intubate-cant.significance: CICO management is crucial for ICU clinicians to prevent hypoxia and cardiac arrest in critically ill patients. Effective recognition and transition to FONA can improve patient outcomes in life-threatening situations.

url:https://litfl.com/adult-intubation-c.summary: This study developed a checklist for adult intubation in emergency situations, covering preparation, pause before intubation, backup plans, and post-intubation care. The checklist aims to standardize and improve the intubation process. It may reduce errors and improve patient outcomes.
url:https://litfl.com/adult-intubation-c.significance: This checklist can be a valuable tool for ICU clinicians to improve their intubation skills and patient safety, especially in high-pressure emergency situations.

url:https://emcrit.org/emcrit/rush-2/.summary: This episode introduces the updated RUSH Exam 2.0, also known as the iRUSH, which provides a standardized map for comprehensive bedside hemodynamic assessment. It combines clinical findings with advanced ultrasound modalities to phenotype shock. This updated protocol moves beyond its original role for the crashing patient.
url:https://emcrit.org/emcrit/rush-2/.significance: This matters for ICU clinical practice as it provides a standardized approach to bedside hemodynamic assessment, potentially improving patient outcomes by accurately phenotyping shock.

url:https://litfl.com/bronchoscopic-anat.summary: This study reviews airway anatomy to help clinicians understand the basics of bronchoscopy and airway management, highlighting normal variations and potential abnormalities.
url:https://litfl.com/bronchoscopic-anat.significance: Understanding airway anatomy is crucial for successful bronchoscopy and airway management in ICU patients, which can impact patient outcomes and survival.

url:https://litfl.com/patient-preparatio.summary: Researchers identified key considerations for preparing ICU patients for bronchoscopy, including time out, consent, and patient positioning. They also highlighted the importance of awake versus intubated & sedated bronchoscopy and effective teamwork. The study aimed to improve safety during ICU bronchoscopy.
url:https://litfl.com/patient-preparatio.significance: This study's findings are crucial for ICU clinicians to ensure safe and effective bronchoscopy procedures, which can impact patient outcomes and reduce complications.

url:https://rebelem.com/abc-vs-tash/.summary: Researchers compared two tools for deciding massive transfusions in trauma patients: the ABC Score, which uses 4 variables at the bedside, and TASH, which uses labs and imaging for a more precise estimate.
url:https://rebelem.com/abc-vs-tash/.significance: Understanding which tool is most accurate can help ICU clinicians make better decisions about massive transfusions, potentially improving patient outcomes.

pmid:42414252.key_stats: n=210, 52.4% developed AKI stages 2-3, moderate-to-severe AKI independently associated with 30-day mortality, VA-ECMO modality and norepinephrine use increased AKI risk, high fibrinogen level and CVD provided protection
pmid:42414252.summary: This study looked at how acute kidney injury (AKI) affects patients on ECMO and found that AKI is a major complication that affects mortality and long-term renal function. The study identified risk factors for AKI in ECMO patients, including the type of ECMO used and the use of certain medications. The study also found that severe AKI is a strong predictor of 30-day mortality in ECMO patients.
pmid:42414252.significance: Understanding risk factors for AKI in ECMO patients can help clinicians take steps to prevent or mitigate this serious complication, which can improve patient outcomes and reduce mortality.
pmid:42414252.rounds_takeaway: Consider using VA-ECMO modality with caution in patients with a history of cardiovascular disease and avoid norepinephrine use when possible.

pmid:42410341.summary: Researchers studied 2935 critically ill adults in a Brazilian ICU to identify risk factors for acute kidney injury (AKI). They found that several factors, including age, chronic liver disease, and high lactate levels, were associated with AKI. The proportion of AKI cases classified as KDIGO stage 3 increased after day 7.
pmid:42410341.significance: These findings highlight the importance of early recognition of risk factors for AKI in critically ill patients, supporting the implementation of kidney-protective care strategies in the ICU.
pmid:42410341.rounds_takeaway: Consider early risk assessment and kidney-protective care in critically ill patients with multiple comorbidities or high lactate levels.

pmid:42087034.summary: This study reviewed the use of seizure medications in patients after brain surgery. The results suggest that using seizure medications may help prevent early seizures, but the benefits are uncertain. Levetiracetam may be a better choice than phenytoin for seizure prevention.
pmid:42087034.significance: This study's findings inform ICU clinicians about the use of seizure medications in patients after brain surgery, helping them make more informed decisions about patient care.

pmid:41916807.summary: This study developed evidence-based recommendations for the surveillance and control of Candida infections using the GRADE framework. The guidance covers diagnostic strategies, antifungal therapy, and infection prevention and control measures. It aims to support clinicians in making informed decisions and improving antifungal stewardship.
pmid:41916807.significance: These recommendations are crucial for ICU clinicians to improve patient outcomes and address the growing threat of antifungal resistance in critically ill patients.

pmid:42481936.summary: Researchers analyzed data from 5721 older ICU patients to identify comorbidity patterns associated with acute kidney injury (AKI). They found five distinct comorbidity phenotypes, with those including atrial fibrillation and ischemic heart failure having the highest risk of AKI. These phenotypes were also associated with more severe AKI.
pmid:42481936.significance: This study highlights the importance of considering comorbidities when evaluating older critically ill patients for AKI risk, and suggests that targeted renal surveillance and individualized hemodynamic management may be beneficial for high-risk patients.
pmid:42481936.rounds_takeaway: Consider targeted renal surveillance and individualized hemodynamic management in older critically ill patients with comorbidities including atrial fibrillation and ischemic heart failure.

pmid:42425561.key_stats: n=10642, primary endpoint: AKI occurrence and maximum severity within 7 days of ICU admission
pmid:42425561.summary: This study aims to describe the occurrence and outcomes of acute kidney injury (AKI) in critically ill patients worldwide. It is a prospective, observational study of 10,642 patients admitted to the ICU. The study will collect data on AKI occurrence, severity, duration, and outcomes, as well as long-term kidney and patient outcomes in selected centers.
pmid:42425561.significance: This study will provide valuable data on the epidemiology and outcomes of AKI in critically ill patients, which can inform future research and clinical practice in critical care nephrology.

pmid:42418363.key_stats: n=202, moderate-to-severe AKI 9.1% vs 11.7%, nephrotoxic drug administration lower in postimplementation period, hypotensive episodes lower in postimplementation period
pmid:42418363.summary: This study evaluated the impact of an artificial intelligence-powered clinical decision support system on acute kidney injury prevention in the ICU. The system, called U-Care Renal Platform, was integrated into ICU workflows and provided actionable recommendations. The study found lower rates of moderate-to-severe AKI, nephrotoxic drug administration, and hypotensive episodes among patients with AKI after implementation.
pmid:42418363.significance: This study suggests that the integration of artificial intelligence-powered clinical decision support systems may be a useful tool for preventing acute kidney injury in the ICU, which is a serious and costly complication.
pmid:42418363.rounds_takeaway: Consider implementing AI-powered clinical decision support systems to reduce the risk of AKI in critically ill patients.

pmid:42409761.summary: Clinical pharmacists are increasingly involved in acute stroke care, but their role is inconsistently defined. A consensus statement recommends their involvement in managing acute ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke in emergency departments.
pmid:42409761.significance: This matters for ICU clinical practice because optimizing the clinical pharmacist role can improve time-sensitive treatment and equity in care delivery for stroke patients.

pmid:41942818.summary: This study developed guidelines for predicting outcomes in critically ill adults with acute ischemic stroke, including avoiding premature predictions and using multimodal assessments. It found that early neurological improvement within 24 hours of revascularization is a moderately reliable predictor of good functional outcome. No other individual predictor was considered reliable for predicting mortality or functional outcome.
pmid:41942818.significance: These guidelines are important for ICU clinicians as they provide a framework for counseling patients and their surrogates about outcomes, helping to set realistic expectations and guide treatment decisions.

pmid:41690564.summary: Researchers created a standardized guideline for using propofol to manage refractory symptoms in end-of-life care by developing a flow diagram and defining parameters for its use.
pmid:41690564.significance: This guideline can help reduce confusion and improve decision-making for ICU clinicians when using propofol to manage refractory symptoms in end-of-life care, ensuring patient comfort and preventing suffering.

pmid:42260906.summary: This study surveyed ICU clinicians and leaders to identify barriers and facilitators to implementing the ICU Liberation bundle, which aims to improve outcomes for critically ill patients. Results showed that clinicians were more familiar with the bundle and prioritized it, but compliance was lower post-pandemic. Workflow integration and aligning the bundle with healthcare goals facilitated compliance.
pmid:42260906.significance: Understanding the barriers to ICU Liberation bundle implementation is crucial for improving patient outcomes, as it has been shown to reduce delirium, immobility, and other complications in critically ill patients.

pmid:42523687.summary: The Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine developed guidelines for treating carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in critically ill patients. The guidelines recommend non-polymyxin therapy for CRE and CRPA, and sulbactam-based therapy for CRAB. These recommendations are based on a systematic review and meta-analysis of 52 studies.
pmid:42523687.significance: These guidelines are significant for ICU clinical practice as they provide evidence-based recommendations for managing carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections, which are major antimicrobial resistance threats in Indian ICUs.
pmid:42523687.rounds_takeaway: Consider non-polymyxin therapy for patients with CRE or CRPA infections.

pmid:42203644.summary: This 2026 clinical practice guideline for renal replacement therapy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury was developed by a Chinese expert panel using the GRADE approach. It provides 34 evidence-based recommendations on topics such as RRT initiation, anticoagulation, and weaning. The guideline aims to standardize RRT management in adult critically ill patients with AKI.
pmid:42203644.significance: This guideline is crucial for ICU clinicians in China as it provides a unified framework for RRT management, potentially improving patient outcomes and reducing variability in care.

pmid:42246225.summary: These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for central venous cannulation in critically ill patients. They aim to standardize the approach, increase effectiveness, and minimize complications. The guidelines cover pre-procedural ultrasound assessment, optimal vascular access site selection, and catheter position confirmation.
pmid:42246225.significance: These guidelines are crucial for ICU clinicians to standardize and improve central venous cannulation procedures, potentially reducing complications and improving patient outcomes.

pmid:41860322.summary: This study developed evidence-based guidelines for caring for older adults in the ICU, recommending a geriatric model of care and avoiding antipsychotic medications for preventing delirium. The guidelines were developed using a systematic review and expert consensus. The recommendations aim to improve outcomes for older ICU patients.
pmid:41860322.significance: These guidelines are crucial for ICU clinicians as they provide evidence-based recommendations for caring for older adults, who are a growing proportion of the ICU population. By following these guidelines, clinicians can improve patient outcomes and reduce complications.

pmid:42272209.summary: A modified Delphi study developed a consensus-based framework for assessing ICU capacity and capability in South Korea, prioritizing functional capabilities over structural metrics. The framework includes 29 indicators across four domains. It provides a foundation for a capability-oriented classification system.
pmid:42272209.significance: This study is significant for ICU clinical practice in South Korea as it establishes a standardized framework for assessing ICU capacity and capability, potentially improving patient safety and resource allocation.

pmid:41773929.summary: This study developed guidelines for using neuromuscular blocking agents in adults with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The guidelines recommend using these agents in patients with a specific oxygen level, but do not make recommendations for other situations due to a lack of evidence. The guidelines aim to help clinicians make informed decisions about using these agents.
pmid:41773929.significance: These guidelines are important for ICU clinicians because they provide evidence-based recommendations for using neuromuscular blocking agents in ARDS patients, which can help improve patient outcomes and reduce complications.

pmid:41773927.summary: These guidelines were developed to provide evidence-based recommendations for triaging critically ill patients during ICU capacity shortages. A multidisciplinary panel used the GRADE methodology to analyze evidence and formulate recommendations. The panel generated one conditional recommendation and five no recommendation statements.
pmid:41773927.significance: These guidelines are crucial for ICU clinicians to make informed decisions during crisis-level shortages, ensuring efficient distribution of critical care resources and saving lives.

pmid:41700745.summary: This study updated the guidelines for managing penetrating traumatic brain injury (pTBI) based on new literature and expert consensus. The guidelines cover resuscitation, imaging, critical care, surgery, and prognosis. A summary of the recommendations and seven treatment algorithms are provided.
pmid:41700745.significance: These guidelines are crucial for ICU clinicians to make informed decisions about the care of patients with pTBI, potentially improving outcomes and reducing complications.

pmid:41655594.summary: This study developed a regionally adapted clinical practice guideline for stress ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill adults in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Nordic countries. The guideline provides evidence-based recommendations for SUP use, including who should receive it, which medications to use, and when to discontinue. The recommendations were developed using the GRADE-ADOLOPMENT methodology and took into account local epidemiology, drug access, and health system variables.
pmid:41655594.significance: These recommendations can help ICU clinicians make informed decisions about stress ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill adults, taking into account regional variations in healthcare systems and patient populations.

pmid:42417792.summary: This study reviewed Brazilian ICU design standards and found they conflict with decades of evidence on environment's impact on patient healing and staff performance. Current standards are associated with negative outcomes for patients, staff, and families. Updating these standards is necessary to improve critical care outcomes.
pmid:42417792.significance: This study highlights the need for evidence-based ICU design standards to improve patient and staff outcomes, emphasizing the importance of policy updates to prioritize patient-centered care and staff well-being.

pmid:42245967.summary: This study evaluated the simplified Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema (RALE) score's ability to predict mortality in critically ill patients with Delta-variant COVID-19 using chest X-rays. The RALE score performed comparably to other scoring systems and remained an independent predictor of mortality. The study suggests that the RALE score could be a useful tool for risk stratification in critically ill patients with COVID-19, particularly in resource-limited settings.
pmid:42245967.significance: This study's findings support the use of the simplified RALE score as a practical tool for guiding treatment decisions in critically ill patients with COVID-19, which could lead to improved outcomes and resource allocation in high-burden settings.

pmid:42518782.summary: This study evaluated the NephroCheck score, a urine test using biomarkers IGFBP7 and TIMP-2, to predict acute kidney injury (AKI) in ICU patients. The test showed some ability to identify AKI risk and need for renal replacement therapy, but its performance was inconsistent for differentiating transient from persistent AKI.
pmid:42518782.significance: Early detection of AKI is critical for guiding timely interventions and improving outcomes in critically ill patients, making this study's findings relevant for ICU clinical practice.
pmid:42518782.rounds_takeaway: Consider using the NephroCheck score to identify patients at high risk for AKI and renal replacement therapy in the ICU.

pmid:42484242.key_stats: n=189, OR 20.8 (95% CI 3.8-114) for stage 2 AKI, OR 93.6 (95% CI 23.4-375) for stage 3 AKI, p < 0.001
pmid:42484242.summary: This study looked at cardiac surgery patients in a single healthcare system and found that 16.7% developed acute kidney injury (AKI). Patients with AKI had higher mortality, longer hospital stays, and reduced renal recovery compared to those without AKI.
pmid:42484242.significance: Early identification and management of AKI are crucial in cardiac surgery patients to reduce mortality and improve outcomes.
pmid:42484242.rounds_takeaway: Consider AKI risk stratification and early intervention in cardiac surgery patients with elevated serum creatinine or decreased urine output.

pmid:42415882.summary: A multicenter survey in Indian ICUs found that 67.4% of respondents were specialists in critical care medicine and 67.2% had received POCUS training. Most used POCUS for lung assessments, volume status, and cardiac evaluations, with key barriers including inadequate training and limited machines.
pmid:42415882.significance: This study highlights the increasing adoption of POCUS in Indian ICUs and emphasizes the need for essential training for intensivists to improve patient care.

url:https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.10..summary: Researchers created a tool called PAUSE-Agents to help with ICU-to-ward transfers by drafting handoff briefs from ICU data and clinical notes. This tool uses a template developed by clinicians and involves multiple agents to ensure accuracy and safety. The goal is to reduce information loss and make handoffs less burdensome.
url:https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.10..significance: This tool has the potential to improve patient care by reducing errors and improving communication during ICU-to-ward transfers, which are high-risk transitions.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: The VA Grant and Per Diem case management aftercare program provides six months of case management for homeless-experienced Veterans undergoing housing transitions. A Partnered Implementation Initiative proposes to implement and evaluate Critical Time Intervention in 32 case management sites. This intervention aims to support housing transitions.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study may inform the implementation of evidence-based case management practices to support housing transitions for homeless-experienced Veterans.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study evaluated the relationship between the CPAx score at ICU discharge and the 6MWT distance 3 months later in patients who experienced prolonged mechanical ventilation and had signs of malnutrition, muscular weakness, or post-traumatic stress symptoms.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Understanding the predictive validity of the CPAx score can help clinicians identify patients at risk of poor functional outcomes after ICU discharge, allowing for targeted interventions.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.rounds_takeaway: Consider using the CPAx score to identify patients at risk of poor functional outcomes after ICU discharge.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study evaluated the effect of structured education for family members of ICU patients undergoing tracheostomy on their anxiety, well-being, and satisfaction with care. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention or control group. The study aimed to assess the impact of this education on family members' emotional and psychological state.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study highlights the importance of supporting family members of ICU patients undergoing tracheostomy, as their emotional well-being can significantly impact patient outcomes. Structured education may be a valuable tool in addressing their concerns and improving care satisfaction.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.rounds_takeaway: Consider offering structured education to family members of ICU patients undergoing tracheostomy to improve their emotional well-being and satisfaction with care.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study is investigating the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of AZD4144 in patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either AZD4144 or a placebo. The study aims to enroll adults aged 18 to 80 years diagnosed with sepsis due to a bacterial infection.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study has the potential to provide new insights into the treatment of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, a serious complication that can occur in critically ill patients.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Researchers induced blood-stage malaria in healthy adults to study malaria development, immune response, and transmission to mosquitoes. The study aimed to understand how malaria progresses in people and how it spreads to mosquitoes. Participants were healthy individuals aged 18-54 from the Washington DC area.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study contributes to the development of vaccines and treatments for malaria, a disease responsible for millions of cases and deaths worldwide each year.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Patients with ARDS were given a treatment targeting CD14 or a placebo. The treatment's effect on oxygen levels was measured over 28 days. The goal was to see if the treatment improved oxygenation by day 4.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study could help us understand if targeting CD14 can improve oxygen levels in ARDS patients, which is crucial for their survival and recovery.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This Phase 2b study investigated the safety and efficacy of TIN816 in patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). Three different single doses of TIN816 were evaluated in hospitalized adult participants in an intensive care setting. The study aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study is significant for ICU clinical practice as it aims to find a treatment for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, a serious complication in critically ill patients.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Researchers investigated the relationship between gut microbiome and enteric signatures in patients with sepsis-associated hepatorenal injury. They found that altered gut microbial diversity and microbial metabolites may contribute to hepato-renal injury during sepsis. However, prospective longitudinal evidence in patients with sepsis-associated liver injury and acute kidney injury remains limited.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study highlights the need for further research into the gut microbiome's role in sepsis-associated complications, which could lead to new therapeutic targets for improving patient outcomes.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.rounds_takeaway: Consider evaluating gut microbiome in patients with sepsis-associated liver injury and acute kidney injury to inform potential targeted interventions.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.key_stats: n=120, Kappa index not reported, p not reported
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This observational study compared the diagnostic performance of bedside cervical ultrasonography to nasofibroscopy (FEES) for detecting post-extubation dysphagia in critically ill adult patients. The study aimed to evaluate the degree of diagnostic concordance between the two methods. No significant results were reported.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Accurate diagnosis of post-extubation dysphagia is crucial for preventing aspiration and improving patient outcomes in the ICU. This study's findings can inform the choice of diagnostic tool for critically ill patients.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.rounds_takeaway: Consider using bedside cervical ultrasonography as a potential alternative to nasofibroscopy for evaluating dysphagia in critically ill patients

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study compared the early warning performance of a NEWS2-based clinical decision support system (KDS) to a machine learning model in predicting sepsis diagnosis. The NEWS2-based KDS provided an alert 4.5 hours before sepsis diagnosis, on average. The machine learning model was externally validated on 2000 patients.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Early warning systems like NEWS2-based KDS can help clinicians identify sepsis patients earlier, potentially improving outcomes. This study highlights the importance of validating machine learning models in real-world settings.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.rounds_takeaway: Consider using NEWS2-based clinical decision support systems for early sepsis warning in high-risk patients.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study investigated the use of fecal lactate as an early biomarker of tissue hypoperfusion in critically ill patients. Fecal lactate levels were measured within the first 12-24 hours to predict poor response to resuscitation at 24 hours. The study found that fecal lactate levels were associated with resuscitation outcomes.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study provides valuable information for clinicians to identify critically ill patients at risk of poor response to resuscitation, allowing for timely intervention.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.rounds_takeaway: Consider fecal lactate levels in patients with suspected tissue hypoperfusion to guide resuscitation efforts.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Researchers studied metabolic signatures in young, healthy ICU patients to understand why some experience poor functional recovery despite being physically fit. They found that non-modifiable factors like age and pre-existing disease only explain part of the variation in recovery. The study aims to identify other underlying factors contributing to long-term recovery.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Understanding the determinants of long-term recovery in ICU patients is crucial for improving functional outcomes and reducing the burden of post-intensive care syndrome.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Researchers used ultrasound to measure body composition in critically ill patients, finding it a valuable and accessible tool.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This matters for ICU clinical practice as it provides a non-invasive and radiation-free way to assess body composition, especially for obstetrics and gynecology cases.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Researchers studied 567 critically ill patients to identify early signs of sepsis. They found that a specific protein, matrix metalloproteinase-3, was associated with sepsis. This protein was present at admission and may help predict sepsis outcomes.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Identifying early biomarkers like matrix metalloproteinase-3 can help ICU clinicians quickly diagnose sepsis and provide timely treatment, potentially improving patient outcomes.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Researchers studied the kallikrein-kinin system in septic cardiomyopathy to see if certain molecules are differently expressed and how they are regulated.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Understanding the kallikrein-kinin system could help develop new treatments for septic cardiomyopathy, a serious complication of sepsis.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study compared standard antibiotic testing to a faster testing method for patients with Gram-negative bacteria in their blood. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either standard testing or faster testing, in addition to standard testing. The faster testing method did not improve clinical outcomes.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This study's findings are important for ICU clinicians as they inform the use of rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing in patients with Gram-negative bacteremia, which can guide treatment decisions and potentially improve patient outcomes.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: Researchers developed a small, wireless sensor to monitor vital signs in extremely preterm babies, including heart rate, oxygen levels, and body temperature.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: This technology could improve monitoring and care for vulnerable newborns, potentially reducing complications and improving outcomes.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study looked at how often adrenal insufficiency happens in critically ill patients and why it's a problem. They found that it occurs in up to 77% of cases, but there's no standard way to diagnose it. Researchers need to figure out how to identify and treat adrenal insufficiency.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Understanding adrenal insufficiency is crucial for ICU clinicians to provide proper care, as it can affect patient survival and outcomes.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study used wearable devices to monitor vital signs in surgical patients not eligible for ICU admission, aiming to detect postoperative complications earlier than standard hospital monitoring. The devices, Portrait Mobile, were tested in patients after major urologic surgery. The study observed the devices' ability to detect early signs of complications.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Early detection of postoperative complications can improve patient outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality. This study's findings can inform the use of wearable devices in surgical wards to enhance patient care.

url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.summary: This study used a new imaging technique to find the best position for patients with lung problems after surgery. They compared lying on the left or right side versus lying flat, and found that one position worked better than the others. The best position helped improve how well oxygen was delivered to the lungs.
url:https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT.significance: Understanding the best position for patients with ARDS can help clinicians improve oxygen delivery and reduce complications. This study's findings can inform ICU practice and potentially improve patient outcomes.
